newsitem.title: POLAND: PBR eurobond not to affect Polish forex.
newsitem.headline: PBR eurobond not to affect Polish forex.

text.p: The Polish Development Bank's (PBR) $50 million Eurobond, sold on Wednesday, is not likely to affect the Polish foreign exchange market, the bank's president Mieczyslaw Groszek told Reuters on Thursday.
He said cash from the issue had already flown into PBR accounts, and would stay on the bank's position so that its existence would not affect the interbank forex market.
"Funds from the issue went into our accounts today, but it will stay on our position," he said. PBR plans to use the cash to boost its currency credit action, he said.
PBR privately placed $50 million of three-year Eurobonds at an issue price of 99.88.
The managers of the issue, CS First Boston and Citibank International offered to investors bonds, maturing November 1999, yielding 60 basis points above three month LIBOR, paid quarterly.
PBR's president said also the bank planned to continue foreign financing next year, most probably through a German marks Eurobond.
